goal.source_text: Maximize downforce while keeping drag under 15 N. You can change the angle of attack, span, flap angle, flap size and endplates.
assumptions: Darwin may change aoa_deg, span_mm, flap_angle_deg, flap_chord_frac, endplate_height_mm; it holds chord_mm fixed.
"Under 15 N" is treated as drag_n <= 15.0 (the limit is inclusive).
chord_mm is not in the editable list, so it stays at its current value of 280 mm.
Flap size is interpreted as flap_chord_frac, which is the only flap-size parameter available.
Held at the current value while the CAD can't change it yet: chord_mm.

design_space.name: FSAE-style rear wing

parameters.name: chord_mm
parameters.description: Total chord, main element plus flap

parameters.name: flap_chord_frac
parameters.description: Flap chord as a fraction of total chord

notes: Ranges from PLAN.md B.5; W-B owns the real solver and may narrow them before CP-B.

metric_catalog.name: downforce_n
metric_catalog.description: Downforce at the design speed (VLM + viscous correction + endplates)

metric_catalog.name: drag_n
metric_catalog.description: Total drag: induced + section profile + endplate friction

metric_catalog.name: drag_profile_n
metric_catalog.description: Section profile drag (NeuralFoil) plus endplate skin friction

metric_catalog.name: cl
metric_catalog.description: Wing lift coefficient on planform area

metric_catalog.name: stall_margin_deg
metric_catalog.description: Section stall angle minus angle of attack (negative = stalled)

metric_catalog.name: span_efficiency
metric_catalog.description: Oswald e from Prandtl lifting-line theory for the planform

payload.rationale: Drag is well under the 15 N cap, so span is the strongest downforce lever per newton of drag. Endplates raise effective aspect ratio, cutting induced drag. Raising both should add downforce while keeping drag under the limit.

payload.explanation: Downforce rose 20.8% (predicted 12-20%, slightly high) and drag rose 7.25% (predicted 10-22%, low). L/D rose 12.7%, though I predicted it flat. Effective aspect ratio rose 21.5%, but induced drag grew only 2.65%. Profile drag jumped 30.9% with the taller endplates and set the drag rise. Stall margin stayed at 4.5 deg.
payload.lesson: Rear wing: raising endplate height inflates profile drag faster than it trims induced drag.

payload.rationale: Drag is 9.99 N against a 15 N cap, so there is slack. A larger flap chord makes the 10 deg flap more effective, adding downforce per newton of drag. Stall margin of 4.5 deg should hold.

payload.explanation: Flap chord 0.3→0.4 raised downforce 10.6% (118.5→131.1 N) and drag 15.8% (9.99→11.57 N), so L/D fell 4.51% to 11.3. All five predictions matched their direction and range. Induced drag rose 22.3% while profile drag fell 10.4%, meaning the extra lift came with a larger induced-drag penalty. Stall margin stayed at 4.5 deg, so the flap stayed attached.
payload.lesson: On this wing, longer flap chord adds downforce but costs more induced drag, so L/D drops.

payload.rationale: Drag slack is 3.43 N and span, flap chord are already at their limits. Angle adds downforce while the section is lightly loaded, but induced drag rises with CL squared and stall_margin_deg of 4.5 falls one-for-one with angle. Bracket to find the drag and margin limit.

payload.explanation: Raising angle from 6 to 7.5 deg cut downforce 1.20% and CL, the opposite of the predicted rise. Stall margin fell 33.3% to 3.0 deg, so the section was past its lift peak. Profile drag rose 31.5%, pushing drag up 2.82% and L/D down 3.91%. Induced drag fell 2.38%, contradicting the quadratic prediction. The stall-margin and L/D predictions held.
payload.lesson: With a tight stall margin, extra angle can cut lift and raise profile drag, so check margin before adding angle.

Stall margin fell 11.1% (4.5 to 4.0 deg), milder than the predicted 15-45% drop, so that prediction scored half. Accepted.

Profile drag jumped 17.1% while induced drag fell 0.956%, so flap-induced flow separation, not extra lift, dominated. Stall margin fell from 4.0° to 3.5°.

payload.explanation: Cutting angle from 6 to 4.5 deg lowered drag 4.30% and downforce only 1.09%, raising L/D 3.35%. Stall margin widened from 4 to 5.5 deg. Profile drag fell 14.3% but induced drag only 2.17%, consistent with unloading a section near its lift ceiling. All predictions held; the verdict is pivot.
payload.lesson: On this wing, reducing angle near the lift ceiling trades little downforce for large profile-drag savings.
